title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Top of page (end of the previous page's argument). Grothendieck works with '½-additive' categories, meaning preadditive or Ab-enriched categories that need not have finite direct sums. Let A be such a category. Let D' be the full subcategory of covariant additive functors A → Ab spanned by finite direct sums of corepresentables h^a = Hom_A(a,−). Restriction along a ↦ h^a gives an equivalence Hom_add(D'°, C') ≃ Hom_{½add}(A, C') for any additive C'. Hence there is a pairing D'° × Hom_{½add}(A, C') → C', (F, G) ↦ Hom_A(F, G). By Yoneda it is determined by Hom(h^a, G) = G(a) and extended additively. It is the 'cotensor/end' companion of the tensor product F ⊗_A G (a coend) defined on the previous page. On the previous page the 'one-object' case recovers the ordinary module tensor product over a ring k.

Main new setup (below the rule). Data:
- a category S;
- a full subcategory C of S_ab (abelian group objects of S), stable under finite direct sums, so C is additive;
- a full subcategory A of C such that every object of C is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of objects of A.

To each X in S one attaches the additive functor C → Ab, M ↦ Hom_S(X, M). This uses the group structure of M; equivalently it is Hom_{S_ab}(Z[X], M). This gives a functor S° → Hom_add(C, Ab). Since C is (equivalent to) the additive envelope of A, restriction Hom_add(C, Ab) → Hom_{½add}(A, Ab) is an equivalence. So the 'cohomology-type' functor Hom_S(X, −) on C is entirely determined by an A-module, namely its restriction to the small generating family A.

Purpose (from the next page): S = Δ̂ = semi-simplicial sets. C is the category of ∂-perfect ½-simplicial abelian groups, or a torsion-free 'special' variant. A consists of elementary objects Φ(i,n), T_n (resp. L^i, Ψ^j). A semi-simplicial set X is thus encoded as a module over a small additive category of elementary coefficient objects. This is a step in the 'dévissage' of ∂-perfect ½-simplicial complexes announced in the title of the folder.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The equivalence Hom_add(C,Ab) ≃ Hom_{½add}(A,Ab) needs exactly the stated hypothesis (every object of C is a finite direct sum of objects of A). If one allowed direct summands rather than sums, C' would have to be idempotent-complete (Karoubian). Grothendieck avoids this by using sums only.
The subscript in 'Hom_C(F,G)' should presumably be A (the category over which the end is taken), in parallel with F ⊗_A G on the previous page. Either the hand blurs the two letters or it is a slip.

ideas.what: Preadditive ('½-additive') category A, its additive envelope D (finite sums of representables), and the universal property Hom_add(D,C') ≃ Hom_{½add}(A,C')
ideas.modern_name: Additive envelope / free additive completion of a preadditive category; modules over a ring with several objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mitchell ('Rings with several objects', 1972); Freyd; standard enriched category theory

ideas.what: Pairings F ⊗_A G (coend) and Hom_A(F,G) (end) between finite-type A-modules and functors A → C'
ideas.modern_name: Tensor product and hom of functors / weighted colimits and limits (coends and ends)

ideas.what: Encoding X ∈ S by the A-module a ↦ Hom_S(X, a), where A is an additive generating family of abelian group objects
ideas.modern_name: Restricted (additive) Yoneda embedding; 'linearization' X ↦ Z[X] seen through a generating family of coefficient objects (cf. functor-category / Morita-type description)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard piece of additive Yoneda/Morita bookkeeping (ends, coends, additive envelope) that sets up the semi-simplicial dévissage on the next pages. Nothing here is new to a specialist. Any interest lies in the surrounding ∂-perfect ½-simplicial project, not in this page.
transcription_corrections: Subscripts read 'k-add' should be '½ add' (Grothendieck's term for preadditive), i.e. Hom_{½add}(A, C') and Hom_{½add}(A, Ab)°.
'noté[?]' is 'noté', followed by Hom_C(F,G) (subscript probably meant to be A).
The first displayed arrow is S° → Hom_add(C, Ab); 'S_ab' there is crossed out.
'C' in the main text is the calligraphic C ⊂ S_ab; the parenthetical reads roughly '(de S_ab stable par sommes directes finies, donc C est additive)'.
Last lines read approximately: 'Or ce foncteur est connu, i.e. équivalent, quand on connaît son image dans Hom_{½add}(A, Ab), donc C est équivalente à celle de …'. The final words are uncertain.
